artifacts.summary: Updated with a 'Post-Completion Defect and Fix' section documenting the manifest registration gap that left the coverage-delta guard inert in production, the fix, and the generalizable source-store-vs-deployed-tree verification lesson.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed a confirmed deploy defect: literature-coverage-delta.sh and literature-term-match.sh were never registered in manifest.json's provides.scripts array, so they never reached .claude/scripts/ and the coverage-delta guard was inert in production despite a passing source-store test suite. Registered both scripts, fixed two related stale index-entries.json line_count values, redeployed, and verified directly against the deployed .claude/scripts/ tree (44/0/0 including all Section H coverage-delta cases).

memory_candidates.content: In a source-store/deploy-split extension system (agent-system/extensions/** deployed flat into .claude/**), a new script's manifest.json provides.scripts entry is a SEPARATE, unverified precondition from the script existing and passing tests. A source-store test suite (run against agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/) can pass 100% while the script is completely unreachable in production, because deploy-headless.sh only copies files that provides.scripts explicitly names (a ~40-entry literal list, not a glob) -- an omitted script is silently skipped, and a consumer that calls it with a not-found/not-executable guard (a common fail-open pattern) degrades silently rather than erroring. After adding any new extension script, run check-extension-docs.sh (its Rule Q: 'script file on disk not in provides.scripts') BEFORE claiming the feature works, and separately re-run the exercising test suite against the deployed .claude/scripts/ copy (not just the source-store copy) after a real deploy-headless.sh cycle -- these are the only two checks that catch this gap; a green source-store test run provides zero evidence either way.

provides.context entries in an extension manifest.json are directory-level declarations (e.g. "project/literature"), not an explicit per-file list like provides.scripts. A new context .md file added under an already-declared directory deploys automatically with no separate registration step and cannot suffer the provides.scripts-style omission bug. When auditing a task's manifest hygiene after the fact, check provides.scripts (explicit list -- can silently omit a new file) and provides.context's companion index-entries.json (which DOES need explicit per-file entries, including an accurate line_count field checked by check-extension-docs.sh Rule R) separately from the context directory registration itself, since they are governed by different mechanisms.
